requirements.finding: Shared Qt/POSIX application and protocol code; current Windows/main is an ancestor. Windows/macOS runtime regressions cannot be qualified on this ARM host.
PipeWire/ScreenCast portal implementation exists. No ARM Wayland session exercised. Preserve existing GNOME cancellation/crash, covered-browser and cadence failures.
Packaged ARM moving-window capture and independent H.264 reception on owned Xvfb. Physical Xorg, other visuals/scales and visibility behavior remain unqualified.
V4L2 ARM MJPEG and YUYV package evidence exists, including busy/reopen/lifecycle. Connected HDMI input is black/silent: moving picture, colors and audible HDMI remain unqualified.

Linux isolates playback streams via Pulse monitors; Windows uses process loopback. Preserve intermittent native PipeWire source stalls during repeated output moves. Per-JACK-client capture remains open.
Private Pulse system mix independently decoded as stereo AAC/Opus. Physical endpoints, routing changes and hardware latency remain open.
Explicit output-monitor selection is implemented and has amd64 evidence; no ARM workflow transfer is inferred.
Selected virtual microphone mixed, muted/unmuted, persisted and retired. Physical microphone quality/disconnect behavior remains unqualified.
Stereo AAC over UDP and Opus over WebRTC verified. Mono, PCM, RED recovery and codec negotiation variants require ARM workflows.
Software libx264 H.264 actually received/decoded. VP9/AV1/HEVC and dual alpha ARM workflows remain unqualified.
Windows NVENC/QSV/AMF versus Linux NVENC/software. Linux QSV/AMF/VAAPI/V4L2 hardware encoding absent. No Jetson/Pi encoder output verified; amd64 GTX750Ti result is not ARM evidence.
Packaged direct WebRTC moving video, mixed Opus, fresh viewer, mute and restart. Public signaling with same-host media is not WAN/loss/browser diversity qualification.
Shared room passwords, HQ/LQ tiers and director controls exist. Protected-room/dynamic tier/authorization workflows require ARM reception evidence.
Shared WHIP implementation and amd64 endpoint/recovery evidence exist. ARM HTTP(S)/TURN/auth/recovery workflows remain open.
ARM UDP/MPEG-TS H.264/AAC and helper recovery verified. RTMP(S), SRT, RIST and RTSP TCP/UDP need ARM receiver workflows.
Spout2 is Windows-only; Linux desktop capture emits opaque pixels. Linux transparent producer sharing and paired OBS alpha receiver qualification remain missing.

Owned-X11 GUI source/profile/audio/mute/Stop/restart/persistence/Quit. Physical desktop, tray/accessibility/scaling variants need evidence. ARM first-run 720p30 versus Windows/amd64 720p60 is intentional and saved selections persist.
Current idle relaunch restores chosen settings. Earlier first-save external-output URL loss remains unresolved; Secret Service failure/lock/reset breadth needs ARM qualification.

Owned packaged live local-control malformed/auth/framing/capacity/deadline recovery cases plus real media observation. MCP integration, headless permissions and broad command/URL/configuration fuzzing remain open.
ARM UDP helper death/stall, source loss/reselection, plus WebRTC receiver reconnect and GUI restart. Physical service/device/network failures remain unqualified.
Native ARM package and portable ELF/ABI/payload/source hashes; Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 userlands on one Jetson kernel. Architecture-separated updates. No universal distro/Pi/installer qualification.
Earlier exact package passed thirty-minute same-host WebRTC observation. Do not transfer it to this candidate; calibrated A/V, native-client and high-motion endurance remain open.
One Jetson ARM64 host; portable and native dependency paths reuse Linux backends. Raspberry Pi, other drivers/desktops and full ARM feature matrix remain unqualified.

supplementalFindings: Windows in-app minidump collection has no equivalent Linux crash reporter; Linux bounded logging and issue export exist.

Windows guide mentions Desktop Studio, Mixer program and independent recording absent from audited native Qt source in both current branch and Windows/main. Documentation/scope discrepancy; not counted as implemented ARM functionality.

Windows guide states 192 kbps audio defaults, while media_defaults.h sets 128 kbps in both origin/main and Linux. This is documentation/source drift, not an ARM-only difference; Windows release runtime is not requalified here.

Preserve linux_performance_validation_checkpoint: one received PCM channel-separation/phase continuity failure and another native-client route-move stall remain unresolved; passing repeats do not waive them.
